column1: # What each published observation stream MEASURES, and HOW IT IS TO BE READ,
# in sentences a non-specialist can follow. The one part of
# `data/build/streams/README.md` that no build can generate: everything else in
# that file -- how many rows, which dates, which columns -- is read back off the
# stream files themselves.
# KEYED ON THE FAMILY, NEVER ON THE FILE. `cases_ituri`, `cases_nord_kivu`,
# `cases_haut_uele`, `cases_national` and their four daily companions are eight
# files publishing ONE quantity in two resolutions for four places. A register
# with eight rows would let the wording drift between them -- one row saying
# "confirmed cases", another "cases", a third silently describing suspected
# cases -- and nothing would catch it, because a sentence has no identity to
# check. There is one row per quantity, and the place and the resolution are
# substituted mechanically from the file the build actually wrote.
# The family is what is left of a stream's file stem once the place it covers
# (`ituri`, `nord_kivu`, `haut_uele`, `national`) and the `daily` marker are
# taken off it: `community_deaths_daily_ituri` -> `community_deaths`,
# `lab_daily_national` -> `lab`, `patients_isolated` -> `patients_isolated`.
# FAIL-CLOSED, ON BOTH SENTENCES. A file this build writes whose family has no
# row here stops the build and names the file, and so does a row whose
# `measures` or `interpretation` is blank. Adding a stream therefore means
# saying what it is AND how to read it, which is the point: a new stream must
# not be able to ship either undocumented or unqualified.
# WHY `interpretation` IS A COLUMN AND NOT A PARAGRAPH SOMEWHERE. Every trap it
# records has already cost someone in this project real time, and not one of
# them is visible in a span, a column name or a row count: that `days_covered`
# does not mean the same thing in a differenced stream and a summed-flow one,
# that a coverage deficit reads exactly like an under-reporting one, that
# laboratory positives include re-swabs and post-mortem confirmations, that the
# community-death column is about ascertainment route and not about location.
# Keeping the reading beside the quantity is what makes it maintainable: it is
# revised in the same row, by the same person, as the sentence it qualifies.
# COLUMNS
#   family          the key, derived from the file stem as described above
#   title           the heading its files are grouped under in the generated file
#   measures        the sentence. Place-free and resolution-free -- both are
#                   stated in their own columns beside it -- and written for
#                   someone who has never read a situation report.
#   interpretation  how to read the family and where it misleads: the
#                   construction the rows come from, what the quantity is NOT,
#                   and what a consumer must condition on. State the limit and
#                   its consequence in the same breath; where a stream is sound,
#                   say so plainly rather than manufacturing a caution.
#   written_from    what the sentences were read against, so they can be
#                   re-examined
# `revisions` and `uganda_exports` are here too, and are the two files that are
# NOT observation streams: they are rendered in their own sections rather than
# forced into a table whose columns do not fit them.
family
column3: measures
column4: interpretation
column5: written_from

column1: cases
column3: How many people were newly confirmed to have Ebola, taken as the movement of the cumulative confirmed-case count the source prints.
column4: BUILT BY DIFFERENCING the source's own cumulative, so `days_covered` is the honest length of the interval a row's count covers and a daily rate is the count divided by it. The weekly file and the daily file are ONE quantity at two resolutions, from the same panel and gated against the same cumulative movement: fit one or the other, never both, or every case is counted twice. A carried-forward revision may land on different rows in the two and both still total the source's movement exactly. The national file is the source's own printed national row and NOT the sum of the province files -- three further provinces and the rows the source has not attributed sit outside them -- so the provinces are not meant to add up to it, and the per-bin residue is in `meta.json` under `reconciliation`. Days the source itself called provisional carry `consolidating` in `flags`; a backlog release lands its whole catch-up on the report day that published it, because the source does not say how it was distributed.
column5: the cumulative case column of the health-zone and province tables, read on every report since sitrep 005

column1: deaths
column3: How many deaths among confirmed Ebola cases were newly recorded, taken as the movement of the cumulative death count the source prints.
column4: BUILT BY DIFFERENCING, exactly as the case family is, so the same three readings hold: `days_covered` is a real interval and may be divided by, the weekly and daily files are one quantity at two resolutions and only one should be fitted, and the national file is the printed national row rather than a sum of provinces. THE DENOMINATOR IS CONFIRMED CASES: a death of someone never confirmed to have Ebola is not counted here at all, so this is not all-cause mortality and not a complete count of Ebola deaths. It says nothing about where the death occurred; for that see the community-death family, which splits by how the case was ascertained.
column5: the cumulative death column, which the zone and province tables gained on sitrep 015 (29 May); earlier dates come from the front-page dashboard tile

column1: cases_notified
column3: How many people the report says were newly confirmed in the 24 hours it covers — the count the front-page banner states outright, not the movement of any cumulative.
column4: This is the same events as the `cases` family measured a different way, and the two must never be fitted together: `cases` is the movement of the printed cumulative over the interval since the previous row, this is the source's own statement of one day's notifications. They agree on 21 of the 22 single-day report days where both exist and part company on 2026-07-22, where the cumulative moved 369 and the banner says 97 were notified; the report's footnote attributes the difference to integrating the harmonised Ituri and Nord-Kivu provincial databases, so those roughly 272 cases belong to earlier days that the source never dates. Every disagreement is listed in `meta.json` under this stream's `vs_cumulative`. A row covers exactly one report day, so it is not to be divided by `days_covered`; `days_covered` here is the gap back to the previous row and exists only so an engine accumulating between rows knows how far it has come. The series exists only for 2026-07-12 to 2026-08-05, because that is the only stretch of the archive in which the source printed a daily figure at all — which is also, not coincidentally, the stretch it flagged as consolidating. Outside those dates this check cannot be run and the differenced stream is the only reading available. `harmonised_declared` is populated on the two rows where the source printed a harmonisation count beside the day's own (2026-07-30, 7 deaths; 2026-08-02, 10 deaths); it is stated separately by the source and is *not* included in the notified count. The province files are the tile's own breakdown, which is the same reading that licensed the national total and sums to it exactly on all 44 case and death readings that carry one. A province the tile does not name carries 0, not a hole: the tile states a total over five provinces and a breakdown closing on it, so an unnamed province contributed nothing, and the reports say the same in words on those days ("Aucun nouveau cas confirmé ni décès"). That is the opposite of the coverage situation in the laboratory and care families, where an unmentioned province is silence with no total to close against. The one report day licensed by the prose sentence alone (2026-07-12) has no printed breakdown and therefore no province files' rows at all.
column5: the front-page banner's `+N nouveaux cas` tile, accepted only where its province breakdown sums to its total or the report's own 24-hour sentence states the same number (scripts/extract_daily_notified.py)

column1: deaths_notified
column3: How many deaths among confirmed cases the report says were newly recorded in the 24 hours it covers — the count the front-page banner states outright, not the movement of any cumulative.
column4: Read exactly as the notified-case family is read, and subject to the same warning against fitting it alongside the differenced `deaths` family. The two agree on 21 of the 22 single-day report days where both exist; on 2026-07-22 the cumulative moved 236 against 62 notified, the same harmonisation that moved the cases. The denominator is confirmed cases, as in the `deaths` family: a death of someone never confirmed is not counted. `harmonised_declared` carries the two days the source itself printed a harmonisation count beside the day's deaths — 7 on 2026-07-30 and 10 on 2026-08-02 — and those are *not* inside the notified figure, which is the whole reason they are worth keeping: they are the source saying in its own words which deaths belong to earlier days. Span and coverage are as above: 2026-07-12 to 2026-08-05 only. The province split is read and licensed exactly as in the notified-case family. Note that Nord-Kivu's books were revised far more often than Ituri's: over the 21 single-day report days, `deaths_notified_ituri` agrees with the differenced province stream on 19 and `deaths_notified_nord_kivu` on 14, the disagreements being small (1 to 9) but frequent. A two-province model should not read Nord-Kivu's differenced daily deaths as a clean notification series.
column5: the front-page banner's `+N décès` tile, under the same licence as the notified-case family (scripts/extract_daily_notified.py)

column1: cases_excluding_backlog
column2: Confirmed cases, excluding the source's declared backlogs
column3: The same quantity as the `cases` family — the movement of the printed cumulative — on every day but the ones where the report says in words that its cumulative holds records belonging to earlier days. On those days the row carries the report's own count for the day itself instead.
column4: This is the family to fit if you want one series and do not want to maintain a patch. It differs from `cases` on exactly one date, 2026-07-22, where the differenced national value 369 becomes the banner's 97 and 272 records are excluded; the province files change on the same date and nowhere else (Ituri 347 to 73, Nord-Kivu 16 to 18 — note that one is *upward*, because Nord-Kivu's cumulative moved less than it notified). Which days are substituted is a reading of the documents, held in `registers/retrospective_batches.tsv` with the source's own words quoted, not a threshold on the size of a difference: a threshold would also have swept up eight zone reclassifications, where the source moves records between places without saying they belong to other days and the differenced value is the right count. The excluded records are scored nowhere. The source never says which earlier days they belong to — the epidemic curve by symptom onset did not receive them on the day the aggregate did — so excluding them is the only treatment that does not invent a date. That is a real cost, stated: 272 national cases excluded, a fixed historical batch against an archive total that grows every release, so it is quoted as a count and not as a share. If you need the total complete, fit `cases` instead and accept that 22 July is misdated, or declare a window of your own; do not expect this family to sum to the source's cumulative, because it does not and is not meant to. `days_covered` means what it means in the `cases` family and both substituted rows cover exactly one day, so nothing about a row's span changes.
column5: the `cases` family, with rows named in registers/retrospective_batches.tsv replaced from the `cases_notified` family

column1: deaths_excluding_backlog
column2: Confirmed deaths, excluding the source's declared backlogs
column3: The same quantity as the `deaths` family, on every day but the ones where the report says its cumulative holds deaths recorded earlier. On those days the row carries the report's own count for the day itself.
column4: Read exactly as the excluding-backlog case family, with the same warning that it does not sum to the source's cumulative and is not meant to. It differs from `deaths` on two dates rather than one. 2026-07-22: national 236 to 62, Ituri 213 to 45, Nord-Kivu 20 to 14, excluding 174 deaths. 2026-08-02: national 50 to 40, Nord-Kivu 23 to 14, Haut-Uélé 4 to 3, excluding 10 — and that day is worth reading, because the source prints the split itself and the arithmetic closes at both levels: the banner declares '+40 décès du jour ... +10 par harmonisation', the Nord-Kivu narrative says nine of its deaths are 'décès antérieurs rattachés rétrospectivement', the Haut-Uélé narrative a retrospective harmonisation of one, and 9 + 1 is the declared 10. Excluded in total: 184 national deaths, likewise a fixed batch quoted as a count. The denominator is confirmed cases, as in the `deaths` family.
column5: the `deaths` family, with rows named in registers/retrospective_batches.tsv replaced from the `deaths_notified` family

column1: community_deaths
column3: How many confirmed Ebola deaths were of people who were never admitted to a treatment centre — found by swabbing the body after death — published beside the confirmed deaths recorded over the same period however they were ascertained, so the two can be read as a fraction.
column4: IT COUNTS ONLY DEATHS FIRST CONFIRMED AT DEATH, which is a statement about ascertainment and not only about place. It equals the dead half of the day's new positive laboratory results on 24 of the 26 province-days where the report prints both, so an ALREADY-CONFIRMED person's death cannot enter it: a case confirmed while alive who later absconds and dies at home is not a new positive, and sitrep 018 records exactly such a death. The column therefore observes the unascertained-infection to confirmed-at-death transition, NOT a transition out of the confirmed-case compartment, and a model treating it as out-of-care mortality among known cases is misspecified. Two further consequences. A community death is inside the confirmed-case denominator too, entering the cumulative case count on the same day. And the boundary is case management rather than location as WHO's DRC definition draws it: a recognised case dying in a hospital serving as a treatment centre falls on the intra-CTE side here, which is how sitrep 081 books two deaths its own narrative calls intra-hospitalier. THE DAILY FILES SIT ON A ROW-PER-REPORT-DAY GRID: the source prints one 24-hour figure per report, so a row is one day of flow, and the report days on which no page classified a death this way are rows holding `NA` in BOTH columns with `n_report_days` 0. `days_covered` is therefore the gap to the row before — 1 wherever the source published on consecutive days — and it now genuinely is the window the count covers, so a rate may be taken over it. BOTH COLUMNS GO EMPTY TOGETHER on a hole. The total the community count is drawn out of is the second column of these same files, `deaths_split_<place>` -- a column, not a file of its own, and there is no `deaths_split_*.tsv` to bind; a model passes it as a binomial size rather than dividing by it, and a fabricated trial count beside an empty numerator would be worse than a hole. Fit it against the total beside it as a fraction rather than on its own, and fit one resolution, not both. The weekly files are not gridded and need no holes: their bins abut, and `n_report_days` against `days_covered` is the coverage statement inside a bin.
column5: the daily ascertainment block, printed as `Décès communautaires` beside `Décès total`; the community column first appears on sitrep 059 (12 July) with no total beside it, so the streams begin on 13 July, the first day both are printed. The ascertainment reading above is the one established in scripts/lib/tablespec.py, where the column's operational definition is worked out from the source's own heading, narratives and arithmetic

column1: lab
column3: How many samples the laboratory analysed and how many of them tested positive — the testing effort behind the case counts, which is what separates a rise in cases from a rise in looking.
column4: POSITIVES ARE NOT NEW LIVE CONFIRMATIONS, and the source decomposes its own paragraph to say so: positives = new cases (alive + deceased) + re-swabs of patients already confirmed. Both reports printing the full form close exactly -- 10 August, 63 = 53 + 10, the 53 being 32 alive and 21 dead; 11 August, 119 = 98 + 21, the 98 being 59 and 39 -- so positives INCLUDE post-mortem confirmations, and across the seven reports that print the decomposition re-swabs run 6.6% to 26.9% of positives. Bind this column to a live-confirmation flow and the model is misspecified; it belongs against confirmations alive plus confirmations at death, less re-swabs. COVERAGE IS NOT REPORTING, and this is the trap that has already been sprung: the laboratory paragraph does not write out every province, so the national files' apparent shortfall against the case series is composition, not publication. Split by `n_provinces`, report days covering three or four provinces agree with the case series to within about a percent, while two-province days sit near 0.76 and one-province days near 0.30; their average is the 0.77 that a downstream model was absorbing into a free laboratory reporting probability, which is a measure of how much of the country the paragraph described and of nothing else. Read the national files conditional on `n_provinces` and `n_province_days`, or fit the per-province files, which need no coverage model at all. THE DAILY FILES SIT ON A ROW-PER-REPORT-DAY GRID, because the paragraph gives ONE DAY'S samples per report: the report days it named no province at all are rows holding `NA` in `positives_*` with `n_report_days` 0, so `days_covered` is the gap to the row before and an engine accumulating between rows scores each day's specimens over one day. `lab_daily_haut_uele` held nine observations up to 20 days apart before that grid existed, which compared 20 days of modelled specimens against one day of real ones. `tests_*` IS THE ONE COLUMN THAT STAYS POPULATED ON A HOLE, at a placeholder of 1: a model divides by it, and a division is evaluated whether or not the row is scored. The weekly `lab_national.tsv` is not gridded and does not need to be — its bins abut, so it has no holes to fill; there the coverage question is `n_report_days` against `days_covered` inside a bin, which is a different and stated thing.
column5: the laboratory paragraph, taken only where the sentence prints its own positivity so the pair checks itself (scripts/extract_lab_prose.py); the decomposition and the coverage split are worked through in notes/2026-08-22-rho-reporting-and-priors.md

column1: patients_isolated
column3: How many people were in isolation and under care at that moment, confirmed cases and suspected cases counted together.
column4: A STOCK -- a reading of how many people were in care at that instant, accumulating over no window -- so differencing it does not give admissions: the difference of two readings is admissions minus exits, and a model that treats it as an incidence will read every discharge as a negative case. IT COUNTS CONFIRMED AND SUSPECTED PEOPLE TOGETHER and the suspected share moves between roughly a half and three quarters, so it does not observe a confirmed-case compartment; `patients_isolated_confirmed` does, and cannot be recovered from this by a fixed fraction. The source keeps printing this tile to the end of the archive, which the confirmed one does not.
column5: the front-page dashboard tile; sitrep 070 prints 766 and its own occupancy table splits that into 278 confirmed and 488 suspected

column1: patients_isolated_confirmed
column2: People in isolation and care, confirmed only
column3: How many of the people in isolation and under care at that moment were confirmed cases rather than suspected ones.
column4: A STOCK, AND THE STRONGEST INSTRUMENT IN THIS RELEASE for the rate at which infectious people are confirmed and isolated, because it reads a STATE rather than a thinned flow: a compartment model relates it to the latent infectious pool directly, with no reporting fraction floating in front of it, which no count of published events can do. Do not difference it into an incidence. Its share of the total census runs 0.23 to 0.53, so it is not `patients_isolated` times a constant. THE SERIES STOPS ON 2 AUGUST 2026 because the source stopped printing the tile, not because this pipeline stopped reading it; what carries the confirmed census past that date is the per-province `care_census_confirmed` files, and those are sparse.
column5: the occupancy table's confirmed column; its share of the total runs 0.23 to 0.53, so it is not a fixed fraction of `patients_isolated`. THE SOURCE STOPPED PRINTING THIS TILE after sitrep 080 (2 Aug 2026) and none of the reports since carries it, so the stream ends there rather than being truncated by this pipeline

column1: cumul_recovered
column3: How many people had been discharged as recovered by that moment, counted from the start of the outbreak.
column4: CUMULATIVE AND A READING AT AN INSTANT, so it is neither an incidence nor a window: differencing two rows gives the recoveries between them only if neither was revised, and this source does revise its cumulatives downward. It counts discharges recorded as recovered, nationally, from the start of the outbreak; a person who left care any other way is not in it, so it is not the complement of the death series. Where a flow of recoveries is wanted per province, `care_exits_recovered` states one directly rather than by differencing. Differencing it day by day is not always a day's recoveries, and one case in the archive is large. The tile sat unchanged at 412 on both 16 and 17 July and then posted 54 on the 18th -- two days of discharges published at once -- against a whole-response sentence stating 22 for that day. It is the only such case: of the 11 single-day intervals with zero movement, the other 10 fall in May and June when recoveries genuinely were near zero (median flow after a zero is 1, against an overall median of 12.5). Intervals spanning unpublished days are a separate and visible matter -- 30 July covers three days because nobody published on the 28th or 29th.
column5: the front-page dashboard tile (`Guéris`), gated against the bare label so a heading is never read as a count

column1: care_census
column2: People in isolation and care, from the care pillar's prose
column3: How many people were in the treatment and transit centres at the end of the report day, confirmed and suspected counted together, as the care section of the report states it in words for each province.
column4: A STOCK, so it must not be differenced into an incidence: the change between two readings is admissions minus exits. IT IS THE SAME QUANTITY `patients_isolated` PUBLISHES NATIONALLY, read from the care pillar's prose instead of the front-page tile, so the national file here and `patients_isolated` are one page read twice — fit one or the other, never both. What this family adds is the province breakdown, which the tile never gives. SPARSE BY NATURE RATHER THAN STOPPED: a province bullet states a census on some report days and not others, so consecutive rows are usually not consecutive days and `n_report_days_silent` counts the report days in between that passed the quantity over. `checks` says whether the passage closed its own arithmetic — `contradicts` marks the report disagreeing with itself, and those rows are kept and flagged rather than dropped, because a contradiction is a finding about the source. FIT THE CONFIRMED HALF, NOT THIS TOTAL. The total is dominated by suspect churn, which is fast and large because a suspect is discharged the moment they test negative, so this series moves for reasons that have nothing to do with confirmed-case dynamics: on 25 to 26 July Ituri's total fell 71 (602 to 531) while its CONFIRMED census ROSE 17 (287 to 304) and its suspects fell 88 (315 to 227) -- the split closes exactly, and the whole move is suspects. `care_census_confirmed` is the series a compartment model wants. AND THIS FAMILY DOES NOT FORM A LEDGER WITH THE FLOWS BESIDE IT: `census(t) - census(t-1) == admissions - exits` holds on only 5 of 21 consecutive-day pairs in Ituri and 6 of 14 in Nord-Kivu, with residuals past 100 people, and the failing rows PASS their own printed checks -- so it is the source's numbers that do not reconcile, not this reader. Do not use admissions and exits to interpolate or correct a census.
column5: the care pillar's per-province bullets and its whole-response summary sentence, filed under the reports' own word `Ensemble` (scripts/extract_care_prose.py); every closure a passage offers is run and recorded, and the printed occupancy percentage is the check that catches a census carried forward stale from the previous day

column1: care_census_confirmed
column2: People in isolation and care, confirmed only, from the care pillar's prose
column3: How many of the people in the treatment and transit centres at the end of the report day were confirmed cases rather than suspected ones, per province.
column4: THE QUANTITY THIS FAMILY EXISTS FOR. It reads a STATE, not a thinned flow: the number of confirmed people in care at an instant, which a compartment model relates to the latent infectious pool directly, with no reporting fraction free in front of it. That is what no count of published events can offer, and it is why these files are worth their sparsity. VALIDATED AGAINST AN INDEPENDENT READER: on all 24 report days where the front-page tile and the care prose both print a confirmed census they agree exactly — evidence about transcription rather than about the counts, since it is one organisation's figures on one page read twice, but a misreading could not produce it. SPARSE, AND MORE SO LATELY: after 2 August 2026 each fitted province carries of the order of ten observations rather than a continuous series, and the NATIONAL file stops on that date entirely, because the whole-response summary sentence stopped on the same report as the tile. Read `n_report_days_silent` before treating consecutive rows as consecutive days, and do not difference a stock.
column5: the care pillar's per-province bullets and its whole-response summary sentence (scripts/extract_care_prose.py), checked against the front-page ISOLEMENT/CTE tile that `extract_banner.py` reads by a different route; the two disagreements over the whole archive are both the sentence's own stated total contradicting its own split, and the tile agrees with the split

column1: care_census_suspect
column2: Suspected cases in isolation and care, from the care pillar's prose
column3: How many of the people in the treatment and transit centres at the end of the report day were suspected cases awaiting a result rather than confirmed ones, per province.
column4: A STOCK, and NOT A COUNT OF INFECTIONS: a suspected case is a person under investigation, most of whom test negative and leave through `care_exits_noncase`, so this observes the triage and testing pipeline rather than any compartment of infected people. Its ratio to the confirmed half moves by a factor of several over the outbreak, which is why the confirmed half is published separately rather than inferred from the total. Useful as a capacity and testing-load covariate, and as the arithmetic complement that closes the total census; misleading if fitted as prevalence. Sparse and intermittent in the same way as the rest of this family, and `n_report_days_silent` states it row by row.
column5: the care pillar's per-province bullets and its whole-response summary sentence (scripts/extract_care_prose.py); where the bullet states the total and both halves the three are checked against each other, and where it states the occupancy percentage for suspected beds that is checked too

column1: care_admissions
column3: How many people were admitted to a treatment or transit centre over the report day, per province, as the care section states it in words.
column4: A FLOW THE REPORT STATES FOR THE REPORT DAY ITSELF: the source prints a single 24-hour figure and this build never spreads it across a gap, so a row is one day of admissions. THE FILE THEREFORE HAS A ROW ON EVERY REPORT DAY IT SPANS — the days a bullet stated admissions carry the count, the days it did not carry `NA` with `n_report_days` 0 — because an engine accumulates a modelled flow from the previous ROW of the stream, scored or not, and rows only on the days the source spoke would make each next row's window as wide as the silence behind it. Nord-Kivu had 1 June and 19 July in consecutive rows before that grid existed: 48 days of modelled admissions against one day of observed ones. `days_covered` is now the gap to the row before, which is 1 wherever the source published on consecutive days and 3 across 28-29 July, the one stretch it did not publish at all. NOT NEW CONFIRMATIONS: an admission may be a suspected case under investigation, and most are — compare against `care_census` rather than against the case series. Cumulative admission clauses printed in the same bullets are deliberately excluded, so nothing here is a running total. Intermittent by nature, and the province bullets that state an admission count are a subset of the ones that state a census.
column5: the care pillar's per-province bullets (scripts/extract_care_prose.py); an `admissions` reading immediately followed by the word `cumulées` is refused, because the reports print daily and cumulative admissions in the same sentence

column1: care_exits
column3: How many people left a treatment or transit centre over the report day, by any route, per province.
column4: A FLOW FOR THE REPORT DAY, on a row-per-report-day grid; see the admissions family for what the grid is and why the file has one. IT IS EVERY ROUTE OUT AND EVERY KIND OF PATIENT: recovered, discharged after testing negative, absconded, died, and in a few reports transferred to a general hospital, over confirmed and suspected patients alike. So it is not an exit rate for confirmed cases, and using it as one inflates the rate by however many suspected patients were discharged that day — net `care_exits_noncase` out first. Where the bullet states the decomposition as well, the parts are checked against this total and `checks` records the verdict.
column5: the care pillar's per-province bullets, where the source's word is `sorties` (scripts/extract_care_prose.py); the decomposition closure is run wherever the bullet prints enough of the parts

column1: care_exits_recovered
column3: How many people were discharged from a treatment centre as recovered over the report day, per province.
column4: A FLOW FOR THE REPORT DAY, on a row-per-report-day grid; see the admissions family for what the grid is and why the file has one. THIS IS THE FLOW WHOSE RUNNING TOTAL `cumul_recovered` PUBLISHES NATIONALLY from the front-page tile: fitting both against the same latent counts the same discharges twice, so pick the resolution the model needs. Read with the death-in-care family it gives the fate split among people who reached care, which is a different and much lower fatality than the outbreak's, because it conditions on having been admitted; charging community deaths against this denominator inflates both. The best-covered quantity in the care ledger, though still intermittent. The national file ends on 2026-08-02 and the province files do not, which has already misled a consumer into reporting that discharge data stops four weeks before the record does. The national row comes from the whole-response summary sentence, which the source stopped printing after sitrep 080; the per-province sentences continue to the end of the archive, and so does `cumul_recovered`. For a province model, fit the province files. Against the front-page tile the two agree: over the 42 report days where both exist the province sum equals the tile's movement exactly on 25, and the 7.2% total shortfall is coverage rather than under-counting -- on days naming one province the gap is +63, two provinces +10, three provinces -4. A free completeness fraction fitted against this is therefore measuring how many provinces the paragraph wrote out, which is the same trap the laboratory family documents.
column5: the care pillar's per-province bullets, where the source's word is `guéris` (scripts/extract_care_prose.py); cumulative recovery clauses in the same bullets are excised before the daily figure is read

column1: care_exits_noncase
column3: How many people left a treatment or transit centre over the report day because testing showed they did not have Ebola, per province.
column4: A FLOW FOR THE REPORT DAY, on a row-per-report-day grid; see the admissions family for what the grid is and why the file has one. AN EXIT THAT WAS NEVER AN INFECTION: these people were suspected cases who tested negative, so they must be netted out of `care_exits` before any exit rate meant to describe confirmed patients, and they are the flow that empties `care_census_suspect` rather than `care_census_confirmed`. Read as a triage quantity it measures how fast investigation clears the ward. THIN: the bullets state it on far fewer report days than they state a census, so treat it as an occasional observation of a rate and not as a series with dynamics.
column5: the care pillar's per-province bullets, where the source describes a suspected case invalidated by laboratory result (scripts/extract_care_prose.py)

column1: care_exits_absconded
column3: How many people left a treatment or transit centre over the report day without being discharged, per province.
column4: SCARCE AND MODELLING-CRITICAL, which is the only reason it is published. Someone who absconds leaves care while possibly still infectious, so this count bounds a route back into the community that no other stream in this release observes at all. But the archive states it on 24 province-days in total, five of them after 2 August 2026, and one published file holds a single row — the Obs column above is regenerated every build and is the whole of it. NO ZEROS ARE PRESENT AND NONE SHOULD BE INFERRED: a report that does not mention absconders is silent, not reporting none. That silence is now a ROW, holding `NA` rather than 0 with `n_report_days` 0 beside it, so the report days the quantity was passed over close the accumulation interval without being scored — read them as holes and never as observed zeros. `care_exits_absconded_nord_kivu.tsv` still holds a single scored row and has no predecessor at all, so its window runs from wherever the model's conditioning boundary sits; it may be unfittable in principle rather than merely thin. A rate estimated per province from this will be dominated by its prior. The care pillar's `Défis` subsection names further absconders attributed to individual treatment centres; those are a subset counted a second way and are deliberately not read, because adding them would double count wherever both appear, so three further report-days' counts are absent from this family by design.
column5: the care pillar's per-province bullets and its whole-response summary sentence, where the source's word is `évadés` (scripts/extract_care_prose.py); the `Défis` subsection is excluded, and sitrep 099 prints 14 in both places, which is what the exclusion prevents being counted twice

column1: care_exits_deaths
column3: How many people died in a treatment or transit centre over the report day, per province — everyone who was in isolation there, confirmed or merely suspected, because that is who the prose exit ledger counts.
column4: A FLOW FOR THE REPORT DAY, on a row-per-report-day grid; see the admissions family for what the grid is and why the file has one. IT IS THE COMPLEMENT OF THE COMMUNITY-DEATH ROUTE: a death here was of someone already admitted, whereas the community-death family counts deaths that were themselves the first confirmation. It is NOT the confirmed-death series — `deaths` counts deaths among confirmed cases however ascertained, from a cumulative — and it includes suspected patients who died before a result where the bullet does not separate them, so it is an upper bound on confirmed deaths in care. The confirmed-only split is extracted but too thin per province to publish. With the recovery family it gives the fate split among people who reached care. It is *not* a confirmed-case death count, and the gap is large enough to misspecify a model: over the fourteen report days where both are stated the prose ledger gives 299 deaths against 205 confirmed, a 46% excess, with the prose exceeding on twelve of the fourteen. Bound to a compartment fed only by laboratory confirmation it puts that excess into the flow that sets the fatality ratio. For confirmed-only deaths in care use the ascertainment split, both columns of `community_deaths_daily_<place>.tsv`: `deaths_split_<place>` minus `community_deaths_<place>` is the source's own printed `Décès confirmés intra-CTE` column, identically, on all 42 Ituri and 39 Nord-Kivu province-days where both can be compared.
column5: the care pillar's per-province bullets and its whole-response summary sentence (scripts/extract_care_prose.py); where a bullet prints the confirmed subset of the day's deaths the two are checked against each other

column1: uganda_exports
column3: How many Ebola cases exported from DRC had been detected in Uganda by that moment, counted from the start of the outbreak.
column4: CUMULATIVE, at the moments WHO bulletins pin, and deliberately unlike every incidence stream beside it: there is no accumulation window, no report-day cadence and no denominator. Two rows bound the intensity of export; they are not a series to fit as incidence, and the interval between them is not evidence that nothing happened in it. Transcribed by hand from published bulletins rather than extracted from the situation reports, so it is the one file here whose provenance is a different organisation.
column5: WHO Disease Outbreak News, transcribed by hand into data/raw/uganda_cases.toml with a source string on every field

column1: revisions
column3: Which published rows were touched because the source revised its own cumulative downward: what the raw increment was, what the stream emitted instead, and how much of the revision was still outstanding after that row.
column4: NOT A STREAM TO FIT. Join it onto a stream file on `stream, column, time` to see which of that stream's observations carry a correction, how large the source's revision was and whether it had discharged by that row. An empty file with only its header is the normal, healthy state and is written anyway, so that a clean build and a missing artefact never look the same. Because the carry is applied to the rows a consumer actually fits, a revision can appear in a daily file and not in the weekly one covering the same days: both still total the source's cumulative movement exactly.
column5: generated by the same run that writes the streams; see the carry-forward rule in scripts/build_streams.py
